title: Decision 18 EXT.COM 5.2: Emergency inscription of the Historic Centre of Odesa on the World Heritage List and the List of World Heritage in Danger (2023)
body: UNESCO World Heritage Committee (18th extraordinary session, Paris; this is a decision of the UNESCO World Heritage Committee, not a court or UN Security Council action)
summary: On 25 January 2023, at its 18th extraordinary session in Paris (24-25 January 2023), the UNESCO World Heritage Committee adopted Decision 18 EXT.COM 5.2. Using what the decision calls the 'emergency procedure', it inscribed the Historic Centre of Odesa, Ukraine, on the World Heritage List under criteria (ii) and (iv) and, in the same decision, on the List of World Heritage in Danger. UNESCO's announcement linked the use of the emergency procedure to the threats to the city since the beginning of the war. The Committee has since retained Odesa on the Danger List in Decisions 46 COM 7A.6 (2024), 47 COM 7A.26 (2025) and 48 COM 7A.32 (2026).
legal_basis: The decision is made by the World Heritage Committee, the body of States Parties that decides which sites are on the World Heritage List and the List of World Heritage in Danger. Decision 18 EXT.COM 5.2 is titled 'Nominations to be processed on an emergency basis - Ukraine' and states that the property is inscribed 'according to the emergency procedure'; UNESCO's announcement says this is an emergency procedure provided for in the Operational Guidelines. The text of the relevant Operational Guidelines paragraphs and of the Convention's Danger List article was not read for this entry, so no article or paragraph number is quoted here. The decision records that, because no site mission took place, assessments of the integrity and authenticity of individual buildings were still needed. Later decisions (46 COM 7A.6, 47 COM 7A.26 and 48 COM 7A.32) call on the Russian Federation to refrain from any action that would cause direct or indirect damage to the property and to fulfil its obligations under international law, including Article 6 of the World Heritage Convention.
outcome: Decision 18 EXT.COM 5.2 (18th extraordinary session, 24-25 January 2023): (1) inscribed 'The Historic Center of the Port City of Odesa' on the World Heritage List under criteria (ii) and (iv) 'according to the emergency procedure'; (2) adopted a statement of Outstanding Universal Value; (3) also inscribed the property on the List of World Heritage in Danger; (4) recommended that the State Party invite a joint World Heritage Centre/ICOMOS Reactive Monitoring mission, if feasible; (5) requested a map and coordinates of modified boundaries by 1 June 2023; (6) recommended that the State Party give urgent consideration to seven points (including extending the buffer zone, reinforcing legal regulation of the Integrated Protection Zone and integrating heritage impact assessment mechanisms); (7) requested a report on implementation by 1 February 2024 for examination at the 46th session; and (8) decided to change the property's name to 'The Historic Centre of Odesa'. Later decisions: 46 COM 7A.6 (2024), 47 COM 7A.26 (2025) and 48 COM 7A.32 (Busan, 2026) each decided to retain the property on the List of World Heritage in Danger; 47 COM 8B.50 (2025) referred Ukraine's minor boundary modification back rather than approving it. The sources reviewed do not state whether the January 2023 decision was taken by vote or consensus.
interpretation: Statements by the parties about the session are recorded in their own official communications. The Ministry of Culture of Ukraine quoted Minister Oleksandr Tkachenko (25 January 2023) as saying the Committee inscribed the site 'Despite russia's efforts to remove this important issue from the agenda' (src_10). The National Commission of Ukraine for UNESCO (25 January 2023) thanked the Committee Chairperson, Princess Haifa Al Mogrin, for 'repelling Russia's attempts to disrupt the consideration of the Ukrainian dossier' (src_09). On the Russian side, the only document read is the Russian Federation delegation's dated amendment of 24 January 2023 (src_03), which proposed, among other things, examining the reviewed nomination under the normal procedure at the 45th session; the sources reviewed contain no statement of Russia's reasons, so none is attributed. UNESCO Director-General Audrey Azoulay said the inscription 'embodies our collective determination' (src_01).
end_date_display: ongoing: the property remained on the List of World Heritage in Danger under Decision 48 COM 7A.32 (2026)

timeline.title: Ukraine prepares an accelerated nomination
timeline.description: Ukraine's Ministry of Culture states that it began an accelerated procedure in August 2022 and that the nomination file was submitted in October 2022. UNESCO states that President Zelensky made the nomination official in October 2022 and that Italy and Greece supported it.

timeline.title: Russian Federation delegation submits an amendment to the draft decision
timeline.description: The Delegation of the Russian Federation submitted an amendment, dated 24 January 2023, to Draft Decision 18 EXT.COM 5.2. The document shows insertions and deletions in a single text (with some duplicated paragraph numbers). Among its elements, it retained inscription under the emergency procedure and on the Danger List, added a paragraph encouraging the State Party to resubmit the nomination under the normal procedure, and a paragraph that procedures be applied to allow examination of the reviewed nomination under the normal procedure at the 45th session, and had the property name changed to 'The Historic Centre of Odessa'. The sources reviewed do not state which parts, if any, were adopted; the adopted decision (src_02) inscribes the property under the emergency procedure, inscribes it on the Danger List and renames it 'The Historic Centre of Odesa'.

timeline.title: 18th extraordinary session inscribes Odesa on the World Heritage List and the List of World Heritage in Danger
timeline.description: UNESCO announced that the Committee, at its 18th extraordinary session (Paris, 24-25 January 2023), 'has used an emergency procedure provided for in the Operational Guidelines' and inscribed the property on the World Heritage List and, at the same time, on the List of World Heritage in Danger. The decision is 18 EXT.COM 5.2; it inscribes the property 'according to the emergency procedure' under criteria (ii) and (iv), also inscribes it on the Danger List, and renames it 'The Historic Centre of Odesa'.

timeline.title: Deadline set for a boundary map
timeline.description: Decision 18 EXT.COM 5.2 asked Ukraine to submit by 1 June 2023 a map and coordinates of modified boundaries, wider than those in the dossier, excluding the port area, and placing the port in the buffer zone. It also asked for a progress report by 1 February 2024.

timeline.title: 46th session retains Odesa on the Danger List (46 COM 7A.6)
timeline.description: The Committee took note of the map submitted by the State Party, which it considered consistent with the boundaries as inscribed; reiterated its recommendation to give urgent consideration to extending the buffer zone and invited the State Party to submit a minor boundary modification; noted with appreciation Ukraine's invitation for a joint World Heritage Centre/ICOMOS Reactive Monitoring mission and expressed regret that the mission could not take place due to the ongoing security situation; reiterated its request for a proposal for the Desired state of conservation for removal from the Danger List, for adoption at the 47th session; requested an updated report by 1 February 2025; and decided to 'retain The Historic Centre of Odesa (Ukraine) on the List of World Heritage in Danger'.

timeline.title: 47th session retains Odesa on the Danger List (47 COM 7A.26) and refers a boundary proposal back (47 COM 8B.50)
timeline.description: In 47 COM 7A.26 the Committee took note of the conclusions of a 2025 joint World Heritage Centre/ICOMOS Reactive Monitoring mission, reiterated its call on the Russian Federation to refrain from any action that would cause direct or indirect damage to the property, requested an updated report by 1 February 2026 and decided to retain the property on the Danger List. In 47 COM 8B.50 it referred the examination of the minor boundary modification back to the State Party, asking among other things for the proposed buffer zone to be extended to the north, west and south of the Historic Centre.

timeline.title: 48th session (Busan) retains Odesa on the Danger List (48 COM 7A.32)
timeline.description: The Committee expressed its grave concern that over 60 cultural sites within the property have been damaged since the beginning of the full-scale invasion, encouraged the State Party to develop without delay a proposal for the Desired state of conservation for adoption at the 50th session, requested an updated report by 1 February 2027 for examination at the 49th session, and decided to retain the property on the Danger List.

approval_note: Approved by Harry Disley in chat on 2026-10-08 after reviewing the batch summary; independent verifier checked against official sources.

changelog.change: Initial draft. Premise checked and confirmed (18th extraordinary session, 24-25 January 2023; decision 18 EXT.COM 5.2; simultaneous inscription on the World Heritage List and the Danger List). Known gaps: (1) whc.unesco.org could not be fetched directly from the sandbox; pages were read through a summarising fetch tool, so only phrases it returned verbatim are quoted and the full decision wording was not independently re-read; (2) the decision pages give year only, not the adoption day; 25 January 2023 comes from UNESCO's news release and the Ukrainian statements; (3) the text of Operational Guidelines emergency-procedure paragraphs and of the Convention's Danger List article could not be read, so no paragraph or article is quoted; (4) not established whether the 2023 decision was by vote or consensus, or which parts of the Russian amendment were adopted; (5) no Russian statement of reasons was found; (6) 46 COM, 47 COM and 48 COM decision days not stated on the pages; (7) the Committee's session report WHC/23/18.EXT.COM/6 was not opened.

Verifier pass. Decision texts 18 EXT.COM 5.2, 46 COM 7A.6, 47 COM 7A.26, 47 COM 8B.50 and 48 COM 7A.32 were read in full on whc.unesco.org and quoted phrases checked verbatim; UNESCO news page (25 Jan 2023, session 24-25 Jan 2023, Azoulay quote), the Russian delegation amendment PDF (dated 24.01.2023), and both Ukrainian statements (Tkachenko quote; National Commission quote) were read in the original and confirmed. Decision numbers, session names/places (New Delhi 2024, Busan 2026), dates (1 June 2023; 1 Feb 2024/2025/2026/2027), criteria and the seven recommendations confirmed. Fixes: (1) 'asked' wording corrected to the decisions' own verbs (recommends/requests/encourages): mission and buffer-zone points are recommendations or invitations, the 2026 Desired state of conservation is an encouragement, not a request; (2) 46 COM 7A.6 report deadline given as 1 February 2025 (the draft implied none); (3) 47 COM 7A.26 and 48 COM 7A.32 summaries corrected to the decisions' wording; (4) Article 6 call on the Russian Federation now cited from 46 COM 7A.6, 47 COM 7A.26 and 48 COM 7A.32 (previously 47 and 48 only); (5) removed the timeline event 'Ukraine submits its state of conservation report, 31 January 2024' and source src_05 (UNESCO SOC page soc/4529): the page returned a bot check and could not be re-read, and the claim is not in the decision text; (6) removed a meta sentence from the summary about the 'premise of the request'; (7) Russian amendment event reworded: the PDF is a marked-up text, and the adopted decision is stated alongside. Not verified: Operational Guidelines emergency-procedure paragraphs and Convention Danger List article (not read); vote or consensus on 18 EXT.COM 5.2; Committee session report WHC/23/18.EXTCOM/6; adoption days of the decisions. No evaluative wording found in factual sections; interpretation section attributes each statement to a named speaker or body.
Approved by Harry Disley; copied to approved/ for import.
